alt_text_recommendation: Ten-slide AI engineering learning roadmap in cream, navy and light blue, with Hammad’s portrait on the cover. It covers foundations, machine learning, neural-network training, LLM retrieval, bounded agents and deployment; then lists portfolio artifacts and a save-and-build call to action.
alt_text_by_slide: Hammad’s portrait above the title “Build your path into AI engineering.” Subtitle: six stages, a working project at every step. A badge says free learning resources.

Six-stage overview: foundations; train, test and compare; training loop; grounded LLMs; bounded agents; dependable deployment. Note: progress depends on starting point and practice, and the path is not a hiring guarantee.
Stage 1, foundations: useful Python, SQL, Git and vectors. Project: clean a CSV and explain each step. Learning sources: CS50P, Python and SQL documentation.

Stage 2, train, test, compare: start with regression or classification, keep a separate test set and check precision and recall. Project: classifier with baseline and error analysis. Source: Google ML Crash Course.
Stage 3, training loop: tensors, a small PyTorch network, loss, gradients and validation. Project: image classifier with explained failures. Source: PyTorch Learn the Basics.

Stage 4, ground an LLM in evidence: tokens, context, prompting, structured output and retrieval with citations. Project: a document assistant able to say it does not know. Source: Hugging Face LLM Course.

Stage 5, give agents boundaries: narrow tools, permissions, errors, state and human approval. Diagram: plan, approve, act. Project: draft an action before executing. Source: Hugging Face Agents Course.
Stage 6, dependable deployment: validated API requests, error handling, logs, latency, usage and costs. Project: a deployed tested demo with a runbook. Sources: FastAPI and Docker.
Five portfolio artifacts: clean-data pipeline, measured classifier, cited document assistant, tool-using assistant and deployed AI service. Add a README, demo, evaluation results and limitations.
Closing slide: “Build one. Then level up.” Save the roadmap and pick a first project. Fine print distinguishes free learning materials from possible hosting, compute, API and certificate costs.
